symbols.doc: Define the editor command :NAME as the procedure PROC applied to the words typed after it. Only while init.scm loads.
symbols.name: define-command

symbols.doc: Define the theme NAME, usable with :theme and set-theme. SPEC is a list of ("key" . value) pairs: base names the built-in theme to start from (mocha when left out), every other key sets one palette entry to a "#rrggbb" colour or "default", and bold-keywords takes #t or #f. Only while init.scm loads.
symbols.name: define-theme

symbols.doc: Start the editor with the theme NAME, a built-in one or one define-theme made. Only while init.scm loads.
symbols.name: set-theme

symbols.doc: True if the command was started from a Visual selection and no edit has happened yet.
symbols.name: selection?

symbols.doc: The selected text: v selections include each newline they cross, V selections are whole lines joined with newlines.
symbols.name: selection-text

symbols.doc: The text of lines START to END of the buffer, 1-based and inclusive, END defaulting to START, joined with newlines.
symbols.name: buffer-text

symbols.doc: The number of lines in the buffer.
symbols.name: line-count

symbols.doc: The 1-based line of the cursor, which is the end of the selection when there is one.
symbols.name: cursor-line

symbols.doc: Replace the selection with TEXT. The cursor ends on the first character of TEXT.
symbols.name: replace-selection

symbols.doc: Insert TEXT before the cursor character. The cursor ends on the first character of TEXT.
symbols.name: insert-text

symbols.doc: Set the status line shown when the command finishes; the last call wins.
symbols.name: message

symbols.doc: Run the procedure HANDLER with each value that arrives on CHANNEL, as a command of its own with a fresh copy of the buffer, until the channel is closed. CHANNEL should be buffered (make-channel n), because a send on an unbuffered one waits for a receiver and the editor never waits. A handler runs when the editor is in Normal mode with nothing pending; until then values stay in the channel. :reload drops it.
symbols.name: on-channel

symbols.doc: A channel that receives #t once, SECONDS from now (0.01 to 604800), kept by the editor. Brote's own (after secs) ends with the command that made it, so use this one to wait across commands: (on-channel (timer 60) handler). :reload drops it.
symbols.name: timer

symbols.doc: Show a window listing ITEMS to choose from, and return a channel. Typing narrows the list, Enter chooses, Esc cancels. An item is a string, or a pair (label . value) to show the label and send the value. The channel receives the choice and is then closed; a cancelled window closes it with nothing sent. Use it with on-channel.
symbols.name: show-list

symbols.doc: Show a read-only window with LINES, a string or a list of strings, and return a channel that is closed when it is dismissed with Enter, q or Esc. Long lines wrap.
symbols.name: show-text

symbols.doc: Ask for a line of text and return a channel. Enter sends the text, Ctrl-U clears it, Esc cancels. The channel is closed after the answer; a cancelled prompt closes it with nothing sent.
symbols.name: prompt

symbols.doc: Bind a key in MODE to the procedure PROC, which runs as a command does, with no arguments. KEY is one character such as "x", Ctrl and a lowercase letter such as "<C-x>", or Alt and a character such as "<A-x>". A key the editor already uses needs OVERRIDE to be #t. Only while init.scm loads.
symbols.name: bind-key

symbols.doc: Run the procedure PROC once, with no arguments and as a command does, after the editor has started and a file is open. Only while init.scm loads, and once.
symbols.name: on-start

symbols.doc: The path of the file being edited, or "" when the buffer has no file.
symbols.name: buffer-path

symbols.doc: The 1-based column of the cursor, counted in characters.
symbols.name: cursor-column

symbols.doc: The mode the command was started from: "normal", "visual" or "visual-line".
symbols.name: mode

symbols.doc: The selection as the list (START-LINE START-COLUMN END-LINE END-COLUMN), 1-based and inclusive at both ends, or #f when there is no selection or an edit has ended it. A V selection runs from the first column of its first line to the last character of its last.
symbols.name: selection-range

symbols.doc: The word under the cursor: the letters, digits and underscores around it on its line. It is "" when the cursor is on anything else.
symbols.name: word-at-cursor

symbols.doc: Where the word under the cursor is, as the list (LINE START-COLUMN END-COLUMN), 1-based and inclusive at both ends like selection-range, or #f when the cursor is not on a letter, digit or underscore. (string-length (word-at-cursor)) is END-COLUMN - START-COLUMN + 1.
symbols.name: word-range

symbols.doc: The first place TEXT occurs at or after the position (LINE COLUMN), as the list (LINE COLUMN), or #f. The search is literal, case-sensitive and does not wrap; LINE and COLUMN default to the start of the buffer, and TEXT must be on one line.
symbols.name: find

symbols.doc: A mark at LINE and COLUMN, 1-based, that stays with the text around it as the buffer changes, so a handler that runs later can still find the place. At most 256 are alive at once; marks nothing refers to any more are freed. Text typed exactly at a mark goes after it.
symbols.name: mark-at

symbols.doc: The 1-based line a mark is on now.
symbols.name: mark-line

symbols.doc: The 1-based column a mark is on now.
symbols.name: mark-column

symbols.doc: True if the text the mark was on has been replaced since it was made, so it only stands for the nearest place. A mark that only moved with its text is not disturbed.
symbols.name: mark-disturbed?

symbols.doc: Insert TEXT at a mark, as insert-at does at a line and column. The cursor ends on the first character of TEXT. Ends the selection.
symbols.name: insert-at-mark

symbols.doc: Replace the text EXPECTED, which must be exactly what is at a mark now, with TEXT. If the text there is something else, for example because the word was edited since the mark was made, it is an error that says what is there and nothing changes. TEXT may be empty, which deletes EXPECTED. The cursor ends on the first character of TEXT. Ends the selection.
symbols.name: replace-at-mark

symbols.doc: Move the cursor to a mark, as set-cursor does. It does not end the selection.
symbols.name: goto-mark

symbols.doc: Replace lines START to END, 1-based and inclusive, with TEXT, which may hold any number of lines; "" leaves one empty line. The cursor ends on the first character of TEXT. Ends the selection.
symbols.name: replace-lines

symbols.doc: Delete lines START to END, 1-based and inclusive. Deleting every line leaves one empty line. The cursor ends on the first column of the line that took the place of the first deleted one, or of the last line. Ends the selection.
symbols.name: delete-lines

symbols.doc: Insert TEXT before the character at LINE and COLUMN, 1-based; the column one past the end of a line appends to it. TEXT may hold several lines. The cursor ends on the first character of TEXT. Ends the selection.
symbols.name: insert-at

symbols.doc: Move the cursor to LINE and COLUMN, 1-based; a column one past the end of a line puts it on the last character, as in Normal mode. It does not end the selection: the selection then runs from where it started to the new cursor.
symbols.name: set-cursor

symbols.doc: Import a module from modules/ beside init.scm; supports only, except, rename and prefix.
symbols.name: require

symbols.doc: Declare the module name, documentation and exported names as the first form of a module.
symbols.name: define-module
